events.headline: Aaron Donald unretires, rejoins Rams on a 1-year, $20M deal to pair with newly-traded-for Myles Garrett
events.detail: Donald announced Sunday (Aug. 30) he's ending his retirement to rejoin the Rams, agreeing to a one-year deal worth up to $20M ($30M with incentives). He hasn't played a snap since the end of the 2023 season; after Los Angeles traded for Myles Garrett this offseason, Donald said the move 'got me thinking,' and he worked out for the team twice (Aug. 5 and Aug. 16) before deciding to return. The two combine for five career Defensive Player of the Year awards and 236.5 sacks.
events.so_what: Pure team-defense angle for this league's points-allowed DEF scoring (+10 shutout to -4 for 35+): stacking a returning Donald next to Garrett gives the Rams' front one of the league's best pass rushes, which should translate into fewer opposing scoring drives even though sacks aren't directly scored. Worth bumping the Rams DEF up a tier on the waiver/streaming boards once the pass rush shows up in real games — not a Week 1 lock given Donald's three-year layoff and no market inputs from actual snaps yet.

events.headline: Jacobs placed on Commissioner's Exempt list to open the season — can't practice or play; Packers trade for Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson as extra insurance alongside Lloyd
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 27 item. The NFL placed Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list Sunday (Aug. 30) while its conduct-policy review continues — he cannot practice or play in any capacity for as long as he's on it, and GM Brian Gutekunst has said a suspension could still follow once the league's review concludes. Separately Sunday, Green Bay traded for Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson (trade terms not yet reported), adding a second body behind MarShawn Lloyd, who'd already looked the part in camp (5 of 7 snaps on the Packers' opening drive vs. Denver, plus a touchdown).
events.so_what: This moves Jacobs from 'suspension risk' to a confirmed Week 1 zero, and likely a multi-week one — he cannot play until the exempt list is lifted, regardless of how the eventual conduct case resolves. Lloyd is still the presumptive first man up on current camp usage, but Johnson's arrival makes Green Bay's backfield a real hold-both situation on this format's 5-man bench for anyone rostering either piece; track practice reps once the 53-man dust settles to see who actually gets the start.

events.headline: Cardinals place James Conner on IR to open the season; Allgeier now the clear Week 1 back, Love's practice status still unresolved
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 27 item. Arizona's initial 53-man roster, announced Sunday (Aug. 30), placed Conner on injured reserve with a designation to return — he'll miss at least the first four games, having never progressed past individual drills in camp while working back from last year's season-ending injury. Third-overall pick Jeremiyah Love (high ankle sprain, hurt Aug. 14) is 'progressing well' per coach Mike LaFleur but still hasn't returned to practice and was already considered unlikely to play again this preseason even before Friday's finale; the team remains hopeful he's ready for the Sept. 13 opener at the Chargers but has given no return-to-practice date. That leaves free-agent addition Tyler Allgeier as the only back in the room currently taking a full practice load.
events.so_what: This format's bell-cow-friendly scoring wants the clarity this backfield still doesn't fully have two weeks out, but Conner's IR stint removes one of three question marks. Allgeier is the real Week 1 starter by default and the actionable waiver-wire priority here (cheap, clear early-season role); don't spend a roster spot on Love until an actual practice report shows him back in team drills.

events.headline: Giants' initial 53-man roster keeps Beckham and Slayton, waives Jalin Hyatt — receiver room settles two weeks from Week 1
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 27 item. New York's initial 53, announced Sunday (Aug. 30), kept both Odell Beckham Jr. (7 catches for 76 yards on 13 targets this preseason, capped by a 3-for-53 outing in Friday's finale) and Darius Slayton, whose own roster spot had been in question after sports-hernia surgery slowed him and trade-market chatter (New York reportedly open to moving him if a suitor takes on salary) picked up this week. The team waived 2023 third-round pick Jalin Hyatt, whose chances were hurt by a preseason injury. Braxton Berrios remains the plan at slot behind Calvin Austin III's Aug. 25 ACL tear.
events.so_what: None of Beckham, Slayton or Berrios move this format's shallow-bench math on their own, but it closes out the post-Austin receiver-room uncertainty — with Wan'Dale Robinson, Malik Nabers, Slayton, Beckham and Berrios all now rostered behind Jaxson Dart, there's no clean vacated-target path left here worth speculating on. A Slayton trade, if it happens, is a landscape note only; watch it in case it changes who's actually active on Sundays.

events.headline: NFL cutdown day moves to Sunday, Aug. 30, 6pm ET — all 32 teams to 53 in one wave, waiver claims due Monday 1pm
events.detail: The league's 2024 rule change eliminated the old staggered preseason cutdown days; every team now trims from a 90-man roster straight to 53 in a single deadline, Sunday Aug. 30 at 6 p.m. ET (moved off the usual Tuesday this year to accommodate the 49ers' Wednesday flight to Melbourne for their Sept. 10 opener). Players with fewer than four accrued seasons hit waivers, claimable by all 31 other teams when results process Monday, Aug. 31 at 1 p.m. ET; four-plus-year vets are released outright as immediate free agents. Practice squads (16 players) begin forming once results are in.
events.so_what: This is the single biggest talent-liquidity event of the summer for this league's $100-FAAB, Tuesday-clearing waiver format — a wave of camp standouts, cut committee backs, and vacated-role receivers lands on the open market Sunday night into Monday, then settles onto the Sleeper wire right before Tuesday's FAAB processing. Worth a fresh /waivers pass Tuesday once post-cut depth charts (Cardinals RB room, Texans/Colts/Bears WR battles, the Panthers and Texans backfields already flagged above) actually settle, rather than pricing off this week's pre-cut roles.

events.headline: Mahomes says knee recovery on track, 'extremely confident' for Week 1 vs. Broncos — but formal game clearance still pending
events.detail: Mahomes told reporters this week he feels 'great' and is 'extremely confident' he'll be available for the Sept. 14 opener against Denver, nine months out from the Dec. 15 surgery that repaired a torn ACL/LCL and ended his 2025 season. He's been a full practice participant since camp opened and hasn't missed a first-team rep, but ESPN notes he still needs to be formally cleared for game action by team medical staff before suiting up — that clearance hasn't happened yet, and this will be the first time in his career he enters a season having played zero preseason snaps.
events.so_what: This league's QB math (league-profile.md §3) prices pocket passers cheap and treats streaming as the default, so Mahomes' health mostly matters to whoever's actually rostered him rather than the wider market — but a Week 1 absence would be the kind of swing that format doesn't expect. Nothing actionable yet; recheck for the actual medical clearance (not just player optimism) as the opener nears.

events.headline: Jeanty still no firm Week 1 timeline, but Kubiak's tone edges more positive: 'we're counting on him'
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 23-26 items. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak, pressed again on Jeanty's low-ankle sprain this week, stayed vague on specifics but shifted his framing: 'We got another week to assess how he's going to look going into this first game, but we're counting on him.' That's a step beyond last week's bare 'on the mend' — it reads as the staff still planning around Jeanty starting rather than already resigned to an opening-week absence — but Las Vegas won't release its first official injury report until the Wednesday before the Sept. 13 opener, so there's still no practice-participation confirmation either way. Mike Washington remains next in line.
events.so_what: Still ThatWasButtery's top injury watch (RB1 by score, Round 2 pick, +45.2 vs. league median). 'Counting on him' is a mild positive over last week's flat 'on the mend,' but it's coach-speak, not a practice report — don't treat this as the all-clear. Keep Washington on the early-week waiver radar as handcuff insurance given the 5-man bench, and watch for the first real injury report next week.

events.headline: Giants' Tyrone Tracy exits preseason finale with a neck stinger, not believed serious — four-way backfield gets murkier at the worst time
events.detail: Tracy sustained a stinger in Friday's (Aug. 28) preseason-finale win over the Jets and did not return, after going 4 carries for 37 yards and a touchdown up to that point. Coach John Harbaugh called it 'not believed to be a major injury' and 'not a serious setback,' with the expectation Tracy is available for Week 1 (Sept. 14 vs. Washington). The injury lands squarely inside the Aug. 18 item's already-crowded room — Tracy and Cam Skattebo as the incumbent co-starters, plus Najee Harris now fully signed and working back from his own Achilles tear.
events.so_what: Not a Week 1 threat on the coach's own words, but it's one more data point that New York's backfield remains the league's murkiest committee two weeks out — this format's volume-friendly scoring needs a real lead-back signal here that still hasn't shown up. Keep Tracy, Skattebo and Harris all priced as shared-touch RB3/FLEX-or-worse until real regular-season snaps sort it out; don't let the touchdown make him look like more of a lock than the room supports.

events.headline: Rams re-acquire Tutu Atwell from Dolphins for RB Jarquez Hunter
events.detail: The Rams agreed Thursday (Aug. 27) to trade for WR Tutu Atwell, sending Miami fourth-round rookie RB Jarquez Hunter in return, pending physicals. Atwell played for Los Angeles from 2021-25 before a one-year free-agent deal with the Dolphins in March; he returns to a receiver room that already runs through Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Hunter had been buried behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum (and possibly Ronnie Rivers) in LA, appearing in five games as a rookie on special teams only. Coach Sean McVay denied the move was a pre-emptive hedge against a Puka Nacua suspension, calling it simply about receiver depth.
events.so_what: Neither player is rosterable in this 10-team, 5-bench format today, but the timing matters: McVay's on-record denial aside, a team stocking receiver depth the same week its WR1's conduct-policy outcome is still pending is a signal worth watching for Nacua (still an open question — see below). Hunter landing in a muddled Miami RB room behind De'Von Achane is a Week 1 non-factor, not a stash.

events.headline: Browns' Todd Monken names Deshaun Watson the Week 1 starter over Shedeur Sanders; Cleveland immediately releases WR Cedric Tillman
events.detail: New head coach Todd Monken named Watson the starter on Sunday (Aug. 24), saying he 'took in the whole body of work over the course of offseason to training camp to games, the joint practice' and felt Watson 'gave us the best chance to move the ball and score points' to open the season on the road at Jacksonville (Sept. 13). Watson returns after missing the final 10 games of 2024 and all of 2025 recovering from a torn Achilles, beating out Shedeur Sanders for the job. Days later (Aug. 27), Cleveland released 2023 third-round WR Cedric Tillman, who'd caught just 21 passes for 270 yards in a diminished 2025 role; the post-cuts WR room now runs Jerry Jeudy as the clear top name, with Isaiah Bond, rookies Concepcion and Boston, and Tylan Wallace behind him.
events.so_what: This settles the QB competition itself (Sanders stays a bench-only name for this format's no-backup-QB doctrine) but doesn't resolve the bigger question for Jeudy owners: a passer coming off a two-year Achilles layoff is exactly the kind of shaky-QB-play risk this league's normal-depth WR math can't just assume away. Jeudy is a confirm-with-live-snaps name, not a locked WR2, until Watson shows he can push the ball down the field in real games.

events.headline: Packers sign veteran TE Jonnu Smith, insurance behind an injury-thinned Tucker Kraft room
events.detail: Green Bay signed free-agent TE Jonnu Smith to a one-year deal Thursday (Aug. 27). The move addresses real depth thinness: starter Tucker Kraft is working back from offseason knee (ACL) surgery but is expected for the Sept. 13 opener at Minnesota, and the next man up, Luke Musgrave, has been sidelined on the Active/PUP list with a neck injury suffered in June minicamp. Smith is one year removed from a monster 2024 with Miami (88-of-111 for 884 yards, 8 TDs) but followed it with a poor 2025 in Pittsburgh (38-222-2 in 17 games).
events.so_what: This doesn't change punt-TE doctrine (league-profile.md §4): Kraft is still the value-price TE to roster if his knee checks out clean, and Smith is purely Green Bay's answer to the Musgrave absence, not a fantasy-relevant name in his own right while Kraft is healthy. Worth knowing only as the handcuff if Kraft's knee has any setback before Week 1.

events.headline: Colts activate Alec Pierce off PUP list, but Week 1 still not locked in; Keenan Allen signing remains the floor
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 20 item. Indianapolis activated Pierce (recovering from March ankle surgery) off the physically-unable-to-perform list Thursday (Aug. 27), clearing him to practice for the first time this camp. In his first session back he did individual work off to the side rather than team drills, a deliberate ramp-up. Beat reporting is split on the takeaway: one line frames the activation as not meaning he's '100% for Week 1,' another says he's 'still eyeing a Week 1 return' — no clean confirmation either way yet. Both Pierce and fellow WR Josh Downs (calf) carried Aug. 30 depth-chart questionable tags but survived final roster cuts.
events.so_what: This is a real step (on the field, ramping up) but not the all-clear — treat Pierce as a contingent WR2/3 price, not a confirmed Week 1 starter, until practice reports show him in full team periods. Keenan Allen remains the near-term floor for Indianapolis' passing-game target competition behind Josh Downs regardless of how Pierce's ramp-up goes.

events.headline: Lions' Sam LaPorta back to full practice all week; hip issue no longer a concern
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 20 item. LaPorta resumed practicing Tuesday (Aug. 25) and continued through the week without limitation, catching passes from Jared Goff in Friday's scrimmage. The hip issue that had coach Dan Campbell declining to guarantee a Week 1 return a week ago no longer appears to be a lingering concern.
events.so_what: This clears the discount flagged in the Aug. 20 item — LaPorta grades back out as a locked-in top-5 TE price in one of the league's highest-scoring offenses, no longer a punt-TE hedge candidate. Draft/roster him at full value.

events.headline: Bears' Luther Burden III returns to individual drills for first time since Aug. 8 groin injury
events.detail: Burden did individual drills for the first part of Wednesday's (Aug. 26) hourlong practice — stretching with the team and catching passes from the quarterbacks — before going inside once team periods started, his first on-field work since exiting practice Aug. 8 with a groin injury. The Bears still expect him to miss the rest of the preseason, with the hope of being ready for the Sept. 13 opener at Carolina. Both Burden and Rome Odunze made Chicago's initial 53-man roster this week, with the club having moved on from D.J. Moore and Olamide Zaccheaus this offseason.
events.so_what: A cautious, individual-drills-only return two-and-a-half weeks out is the expected shape of this recovery, not a setback — Burden was ticketed as Chicago's post-DJ Moore-trade WR1 target earner, and this keeps him on track as a normal-depth WR2/FLEX price for this format rather than a bench stash. Recheck for a move into full team drills before locking in a clean Week 1 grade.

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase hyperextends knee at Bengals practice, sits out Wednesday as a precaution
events.detail: Chase went down after landing awkwardly on a route from Joe Burrow in Tuesday's (Aug. 25) practice, immediately grabbing his left knee, but walked off under his own power and did not return. He called it a minor hyperextension and said, 'If I had a game tomorrow, I would play.' Cincinnati held him out of Wednesday's (Aug. 26) practice in what's being described as a precautionary move, and he won't play in Friday's preseason finale against Philadelphia.
events.so_what: Chase is this format's clearest elite-WR price (league-profile.md §1's 'elite is worth more than consensus' logic) — a scare with the player himself saying he'd play in a real game, followed by a single precautionary sit, is the good version of this story, not a Week 1 threat. No price adjustment needed; just confirm there's no setback before the opener.

events.headline: Puka Nacua's civil case gets a trial date of March 2028; NFL suspension still an open question, not resolved before Week 1
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 15 item. A Los Angeles County judge has now set a trial date of March 27, 2028 for the civil lawsuit alleging assault and battery against Nacua, meaning the legal case itself will not resolve anywhere near this season. Nacua was not included in the NFL's most recent batch of suspensions, but that does not clear him — Schefter has reported the league's own conduct-policy review is separate from and does not wait on the civil trial, and as of Aug. 30 Schefter says the NFL still has no obligation to rule before Week 1. One mitigating factor for any league discipline: Nacua reportedly checked himself into rehab on his own following the incident.
events.so_what: Nacua is bwalsh89's roster now, not a draft-price question — with the civil trial pushed out to 2028, any 2026 discipline risk comes entirely from the NFL's own conduct review, which could land at any point in the season with no advance warning, Week 1 included. Keep him started as the elite-WR asset he is, but check for a league ruling each week rather than assuming the quiet stretch since the last suspension batch means he's clear.

events.headline: Texans' post-Boutte-trade depth chart settles: Collins/Boutte are the outside starters, Hutchinson and Noel bumped to depth
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 19-20 items on Jayden Higgins' season-ending ACL tear. Houston acquired WR Kayshon Boutte from New England on Monday (Aug. 24) for a 2028 seventh-round pick and second-year safety Jaylen Reed. The Texans' first post-trade depth chart lists Nico Collins as WR1 and Boutte as the new WR2, with Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Tank Dell bumped down to depth/rotational roles rather than settled starting jobs; all four (Collins, Boutte, Hutchinson, Noel) survived Sunday's (Aug. 30) roster cuts as locks for the 53.
events.so_what: This resolves the ambiguity flagged when the trade first broke — Boutte, not Hutchinson or Noel, is the immediate answer to the Higgins vacancy, and this format's shallow bench has no room to speculatively roster either bumped-down piece. Boutte himself is still a confirm-before-trusting name in this normal-depth-at-WR math now that final cuts have kept the room intact — track him through the first couple of Week 1 game plans before pricing him for lineup or waiver purposes.

events.headline: Canales confirms Panthers will open the season with a genuine Hubbard/Brooks committee, not a hierarchy
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 21 item. Coach Dave Canales said Sunday (Aug. 24) the plan, assuming Hubbard is healthy, is a series-based split: 'You have a lead back for the series, the other guy comes in on third down so they can be in there for the protection... whoever the lead guy for the base downs is, they'll get the bulk of that rhythm.' Hubbard (hamstring) is still expected back for Week 1 but hasn't played a preseason snap; Brooks has looked increasingly healthy this camp after an injury-plagued start to his career. Both backs, plus Trevor Etienne, survived Sunday's (Aug. 30) roster cuts.
events.so_what: This is Canales on the record ruling out a clean bell-cow outcome in Carolina for Week 1 at least — this format's bell-cow-friendly scoring rewards exactly the outcome this denies, so neither back should be priced as a set-and-forget starter until real snap counts show who gets the 'base down' lead role. Track early-season usage closely for both rosters.

events.headline: 49ers activate George Kittle off PUP, suits up for first padded practice since Achilles tear
events.detail: San Francisco activated Kittle from the physically unable to perform list Sunday (Aug. 23), letting him do individual work in full pads for the first time since tearing his right Achilles in the Jan. 11 playoff loss to Philadelphia. Kittle says he's 'very confident' he avoids opening the year on PUP and still has a shot at Week 1 against the Rams in Australia, but conceded missing that game and playing Week 2 instead 'is what it is' — the activation guarantees he's eligible to play within the first four weeks regardless.
events.so_what: TE doctrine here is elite-at-a-discount or punt, never the middle (league-profile.md §4) — Kittle off PUP and in pads seven months post-tear is the clearest green light yet for treating him as a real Week 1-or-2 threat rather than a straight punt, worth a mid-round flier at a discount to his healthy ADP. Recheck for an actual practice-participation report (individual vs. full team drills) before pricing him as clean.

events.headline: McCaffrey back at full team drills Sunday, taking carries for first time since Aug. 10 tightness
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 20 item. McCaffrey returned to 49ers practice Sunday (Aug. 23) after missing roughly two weeks with the 'tightness' that sidelined him since Aug. 10, and this time he's doing more than warmups — multiple reporters' video shows him going through individual drills and getting carries in team periods. Participation levels aren't officially announced this time of year, but the on-field work is a clear step up from last week's pregame-only movement. TE George Kittle was activated off PUP the same day (see prior item).
events.so_what: This is the clearest positive signal yet for this format's cleanest bell-cow RB1 price — actual carries in team drills, not just warmup movement, is a real de-risking after two lost weeks of camp. Price him at his normal RB1 level; the missed-practice discount from the Aug. 19-20 items should now come off.

events.headline: Broncos' RJ Harvey hauls in 21-yard wheel-route TD from Bo Nix; Dobbins held out for a second straight game with a real soft-tissue issue, not just a rest day
events.detail: Updates the Aug. 15 item. In Friday's (Aug. 21) preseason Week 2 loss to Green Bay, Harvey took the Broncos' opening-drive first-team reps and caught a 21-yard touchdown on a wheel route from Bo Nix. J.K. Dobbins was again held out — but reporting through camp clarifies this isn't simple load management: Dobbins first left an Aug. 10 practice with a coach-confirmed soft-tissue injury (one of several Broncos to be hit by the issue, along with WRs Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims), was back in full pads days later looking sharp, but was still held out of Friday's game as the team manages a lingering issue rather than a clean bill of health. Coach Sean Payton has said the staff wants to get Harvey more work between the tackles after a modest opener.
events.so_what: A second straight week of clean first-team-with-starters usage while the presumptive early-down complement sits out preseason with an actual (if minor) injury, not just rest, is a strong role signal — Harvey's receiving-TD profile plays well in this league's half-PPR/2-FLEX math. Hold him at his early-round RB price as the lead back, and treat Dobbins as a genuine hold-until-practicing name rather than a healthy scratch.

events.headline: Texans' Woody Marks scores on 20-yard TD run with Montgomery rested; backfield shaping up as lead-back-plus-passing-down-complement
events.detail: Marks started in place of a rested David Montgomery in Thursday's (Aug. 20) preseason Week 2 loss to the Raiders, rushing 4 times for 37 yards (including the 20-yard score) and adding a 6-yard catch. Per NFL Network's Jane Slater, the Texans plan 'meaningful roles' for both backs, with Montgomery getting 'slightly' more work and the staff using personnel groupings to get Marks involved, especially on third downs and in the passing game, more than his rookie 2025 usage.
events.so_what: This format's bell-cow-friendly scoring rewards Montgomery's presumptive lead-back, goal-line role over Marks' complementary passing-down job, so Montgomery is the safer RB2/FLEX price while Marks profiles as a change-of-pace flier with 2-FLEX-relevant PPR-adjacent value only if Montgomery falters. Not a true even committee, but not a clean bell cow either.

events.headline: Saints' Alvin Kamara suffers MCL sprain, out at least a month; Etienne set for workhorse role; IR stint possible
events.detail: Kamara sustained an MCL sprain during Tuesday's (Aug. 18) joint-practice scrimmage against the Cowboys. ESPN's Adam Schefter reports he'll miss at least a month, a timeline that puts the Sept. 7 regular-season opener and likely Week 2 in jeopardy. Travis Etienne, signed this offseason as the Saints' presumptive lead back for the post-Kamara transition, is now positioned to handle a workhorse-level early-down and passing-down role in his absence; behind him the depth chart runs Kendre Miller, Devin Neal and Audric Estime, none likely to matter in this format. Assuming the sprain follows the pattern of Kamara's past knee injuries, the recovery could stretch to four-to-six weeks; the Saints' Week 2 game at Baltimore sits right at the early end of that window (32 days out), and the team is expected to let his recovery play out before setting a firm return target, leaving a season-opening IR stint on the table.
events.so_what: This format's bell-cow-friendly half-PPR/2-FLEX math rewards exactly this kind of touch consolidation — Etienne jumps from committee-adjacent to a clean top-20 overall price for as long as Kamara is out, while Kamara himself is a tough hold on a 5-man bench: he won't play Week 1, may not be ready for Week 2 either, and may not be healthy enough to roster over a streamer until his practice status clears — an IR stash is a real possibility once the Saints finalize their 53. Treat Etienne like the workhorse he's about to become, not the committee back his ADP still reflects.

events.headline: Giants officially sign Najee Harris to one-year deal, release JuJu Smith-Schuster
events.detail: New York made it official Tuesday (Aug. 18), signing free-agent RB Najee Harris to a one-year contract after his Monday workout impressed coach John Harbaugh, and releasing WR JuJu Smith-Schuster in a corresponding move. Harris rushed for 1,000+ yards in each of his four seasons in Pittsburgh before tearing his Achilles three games into a 2025 stint with the Chargers; he's now working back into a Giants backfield that already lists Skattebo and Tracy as co-starters on the Aug. 12 depth chart, plus Devin Singletary.
events.so_what: A completed signing, not just a visit, is a real bearish read for both Skattebo and Tracy in this format's volume-friendly scoring: a genuine veteran addition, even on a prove-it deal and coming off a major injury, further muddies an already-even co-starter split. Don't lock either incumbent into a set draft-round price until real preseason snaps show who's actually getting the Week 1 bulk of touches, now a three-way question at minimum.

events.headline: Jets' Breece Hall: MRI confirms groin strain, Jets 'dodge worst-case scenario'
events.detail: Hall left Monday's (Aug. 17) practice early with a groin strain after going down untouched following a catch on rain-slicked grass. An MRI Tuesday (Aug. 18) confirmed the shared diagnosis of a strain rather than something more severe, and beat coverage frames it as sidelining him roughly two-to-three weeks and out for the rest of the preseason, with an optimistic outlook for the Week 1 opener. Coach Aaron Glenn had already downplayed it same-day ('I don't think it was a big deal'), and the imaging result backs that read.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 17 item — the MRI confirming a straightforward strain (not a tear) keeps Hall priced as this format's clean bell-cow RB1/2 off a 1,065-yard, 36-catch 2025, though missing the rest of the preseason is a real accumulation of lost camp reps. Recheck for an actual return-to-practice date rather than pricing him at a full discount or a full clean grade off imaging alone.
